title: Fault Escaping: Improving Robustness of DPU Enhanced Platform with Mutual Assisted VM Recovery
problem: Modern cloud servers that use DPUs to offload virtualization split VM state across the DPU SoC and the host, so a failure in either component crashes the entire machine and all hosted VMs, with no fault-tolerant mechanism designed for this split-hypervisor architecture.
motivation: DPU-based offloading has increased cloud server failure rates because the split of hypervisor functions across two processing units doubles the failure surface, requiring a fundamental rethink of VM fault tolerance.
method: The approach treats the DPU chip and host server as redundant peers using a hybrid synchronization protocol. This protocol keeps each VM's complete state mirrored on both components with minimal overhead (kilobytes per VM), smartly prioritizing frequently-changing VM data (hot state) over rarely-changing data (cold state) to reduce bandwidth. When one component fails, the VMs immediately resume on the other side instead of waiting for the failed component to recover.
key_novelty: The system maintains complete VM state on both the DPU and host, treating them as redundant peers, so virtual machines can instantly escape to whichever component is still working.
contributions: Fault-escaping scheme that enables VM migration from a failing DPU or host to the surviving peer
Hybrid synchronization protocol maintaining full VM state accessibility on both sides with kilobyte-scale overhead
VM state verification mechanism ensuring only a consistent, uncorrupted state is migrated
Improved cloud server robustness without requiring dedicated fault-recovery hardware

metrics.other: kilobytes of synchronization overhead (vs. full VM state transfer); VM recovery latency improvement (exact numbers not available from abstract)

limitations: Recovery requires the surviving peer to have sufficient resources to host the migrated VMs; peer resource contention under simultaneous failures is not discussed.
primary_theme: VM fault tolerance via peer redundancy in DPU-split hypervisor architectures
